chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Nusayr Abu al-Hakam al-Khath'ami, from Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), who said:
The believer is of two (types of) believers. So there is a believer who ratified the Covenant of Allah and was loyal to His Stipulation, and that is in the Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic:
[33:23] From the Believers are men who ratified what Covenant Allah Made with them.
So that is the one who would not be struck by the horrors of the world nor the horrors of the Hereafter, and that is from those who intercede and are not in need of being interceded for.

And there is a believer like the stalk of the crop — sometimes it bends and sometimes it stands upright. So that is from those who would be struck by the horrors of the world and the horrors of the Hereafter, and that is from those who would be interceded for and who would not (themselves) intercede.

key_terms.أَهْوَالُ: horrors/terrors — the dreadful trials and afflictions of both this world and the Hereafter
key_terms.خَامَةِ الزَّرْعِ: stalk of the crop — a metaphor for the spiritually inconsistent believer who alternates between rectitude and deviation
key_terms.شَرْطِهِ: His Stipulation — the conditions and obligations attached to the Divine Covenant
key_terms.عَهْدِ اللَّهِ: the Covenant of Allah — the binding divine pact that defines the highest rank of iman
key_terms.مُؤْمِنَانِ: two (types of) believers — the Imam's dual classification of the ranks of the faithful
key_terms.يَشْفَعُ: intercedes — exercises shafa'ah on behalf of others before Allah on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.يُشْفَعُ لَهُ: is interceded for — is the recipient of another's shafa'ah rather than its agent

ai.seo_question: What are the two types of believers (Mumineen) according to Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) in al-Kafi, and how do they differ in intercession on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Imam Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) divides believers into two ranks: the steadfast believer who fulfills the Divine Covenant — as referenced in Quran 33:23 — and who is thereby shielded from the terrors of both this world and the Hereafter, possessing the rank to intercede for others without requiring intercession. The second is the wavering believer, likened to a plant stalk that bends and then straightens, who remains susceptible to worldly and eschatological tribulations and depends upon the intercession of others for salvation.
